title: Using Outside Knowledge In Reading
content: In Reading, answer only from the passage. Outside knowledge can make a statement seem true, but IELTS marks based on textual evidence. Always ask whether the passage explicitly supports, contradicts, or does not mention the claim.

title: Overusing Memorized Writing Templates
content: Templates can help structure an answer, but overusing memorized phrases can make ideas sound unnatural or irrelevant. A better approach is to keep a simple paragraph structure and adapt your language to the exact question.

title: Choosing The First Listening Option
content: In Listening, speakers often mention an option and then reject or correct it. Do not write the first answer too quickly. Listen for signals such as actually, no, sorry, instead, or what I mean is.
